title: Philippine & Bikolano Art Forms, Artists vs. Artisans, GAMABA & National Artists
subject: Arts Appreciation
description: 8 major Philippine art forms, Bikolano traditions (Pantomina, Peñafrancia, Abaca), Artist vs. Artisan (Amorsolo, Juan Luna, Tina Maristela-Ocampo), GAMABA (RA 7355 & all Living Treasures), and Order of National Artists.
sourceFile: midterm reviewer.docx, ART APPRECIATION REVIEWER - FINAL EXAMINATION.pdf

questions.question: Which category of Philippine art combines artistic creativity with objects that serve a practical everyday function, such as weaving, pottery, basketry, and woodcarving?
questions.explanation: Applied arts merge artistic design and craftsmanship with functional objects like textiles, pottery, furniture, and basketry.

questions.question: Kulintang and Gangsa ensembles belong to which major Philippine art form?
questions.explanation: Kulintang and Gangsa are traditional Philippine instrumental music traditions.

questions.question: Traditional theatrical forms like Senakulo and Sarswela fall under which Philippine art form?
questions.explanation: Senakulo and Sarswela are staged dramatic storytelling performances categorized under Theater.

questions.question: Pantomina, also known as the 'Dance of the Doves,' is a traditional courtship dance strongly associated with which Philippine region?
questions.explanation: Pantomina is a signature Bikolano courtship dance inspired by the movements of doves.

questions.question: Which major religious festival in Naga City brings together religious processions, music, dance, costumes, decorations, and performances?
questions.explanation: The Peñafrancia Festival in Naga City is a prominent Bikolano religious and festival art tradition combining multiple art forms.

questions.question: Bicol is especially renowned for handicrafts, bags, ropes, and woven goods made from abaca fiber, which is derived from what plant?
questions.explanation: Abaca fiber comes from Musa textilis and connects nature, livelihood, craftsmanship, and Bikolano cultural identity.

questions.question: When using the Question Guide to appreciate indigenous art, asking 'HOW is it connected to the community's beliefs, environment, livelihood, or identity?' helps avoid:
options: Dismissing indigenous art as merely 'old-fashioned' or purely decorative
Measuring the dimensions of a basket
questions.answer: Dismissing indigenous art as merely 'old-fashioned' or purely decorative
questions.explanation: Indigenous arts are living systems of knowledge, belief, and identity that must be understood within their cultural context.

questions.question: What is the primary distinction between an artist and an artisan?
options: Artists never work with physical materials, while artisans only paint landscapes.
Artists emphasize creative expression and ideas (indirectly functional fine arts), while artisans emphasize specialized craftsmanship producing functional or decorative objects.
Artisans are strictly unpaid volunteers, while artists only work in films.
Artists cannot receive national awards, while artisans can.
questions.answer: Artists emphasize creative expression and ideas (indirectly functional fine arts), while artisans emphasize specialized craftsmanship producing functional or decorative objects.
questions.explanation: Though the two roles can overlap, artists emphasize expressive/conceptual creation while artisans emphasize specialized craft mastery.

questions.question: Which painter is celebrated as the 'Grand Old Man of Philippine Art,' became the very first National Artist in 1972, and was famed for rural landscapes, Dalagang Filipina, and backlighting?
questions.explanation: Fernando Cueto Amorsolo (born May 30, 1892) was the sole 1972 National Artist for Visual Arts, renowned for sunlit rural scenes and backlighting.

questions.question: Which masterpiece by Juan Luna won three gold medals at the Exposición Nacional de Bellas Artes in 1884 and inspired José Rizal's speech 'The Glorification of Genius'?
questions.explanation: Juan Luna's 1884 Neoclassical/Romantic-Realist painting Spoliarium is housed at the National Museum of the Philippines.

questions.question: Filipino artisan Tina Maristela-Ocampo founded which brand to showcase handmade bags crafted from local indigenous materials by Filipino artisans?
questions.explanation: Tina Maristela-Ocampo conceptualized Celestina to 'bring whatever is here in the Philippines out to the world' through artisan-crafted bags.

questions.question: What does GAMABA stand for, and what law institutionalized it in 1992?
options: Gawad sa Manlilikha ng Bayan; Republic Act No. 7355
Gawad ng Makabayang Alagad; Republic Act No. 1425
Grupo ng mga Alagad ng Sining; Republic Act No. 9155
Gawad para sa Modernong Arkitektura; Executive Order No. 200
questions.answer: Gawad sa Manlilikha ng Bayan; Republic Act No. 7355
questions.explanation: GAMABA (National Living Treasures Award) was institutionalized on April 3, 1992 under RA 7355, administered by the NCCA.

questions.question: To qualify as a Manlilikha ng Bayan (GAMABA), the folk art tradition practiced by the candidate must have been in existence and documented for at least:
questions.explanation: Candidates must engage in a folk art tradition documented for at least 50 years and pass on their skills to community members.

questions.question: Who spearheaded the institutionalization of GAMABA, and which Philippine president signed RA 7355 into law?
options: Felipe M. de Leon, Jr.; Corazon C. Aquino
questions.answer: Felipe M. de Leon, Jr.; Corazon C. Aquino
questions.explanation: NCCA chairman Felipe M. de Leon, Jr. spearheaded GAMABA, and President Corazon C. Aquino signed RA 7355 on April 3, 1992.

questions.question: What incentives are granted to a GAMABA awardee under RA 7355 and NCCA provisions?
options: A plaque only, with no financial support
A specially designed medallion, ₱100,000 initial grant, lifetime monthly stipend/allowance, and up to ₱750,000 annual medical benefit
A diplomatic passport and seat in Congress
questions.answer: A specially designed medallion, ₱100,000 initial grant, lifetime monthly stipend/allowance, and up to ₱750,000 annual medical benefit
questions.explanation: Awardees receive a medallion, ₱100,000 initial grant, ₱10,000 monthly stipend (increased via ₱14,000 allowance), up to ₱750,000/year medical benefit, and funeral honors.

questions.question: Which 1998 GAMABA awardee from Lake Sebu, South Cotabato was honored for her mastery of T'boli t'nalak abaca ikat weaving?
questions.explanation: Lang Dulay was recognized in 1998 for preserving T'boli t'nalak weaving.

questions.question: Ginaw Bilog (1993 GAMABA awardee) from Oriental Mindoro was recognized for preserving:
options: Hanunuo Mangyan script and ambahan/ambalan poetry
questions.answer: Hanunuo Mangyan script and ambahan/ambalan poetry
questions.explanation: Ginaw Bilog preserved the Hanunuo Mangyan script and traditional poetry for posterity.

questions.question: Samaon Sulaiman of Maguindanao received the 1993 GAMABA award for his mastery of which difficult two-stringed plucked lute?
questions.explanation: Samaon Sulaiman was acclaimed for his mastery of the Magindanao kutyapi.

questions.question: Which 1993 GAMABA awardee from Brookes Point, Palawan was honored for his mastery of the basal gong ensemble and the kulilal and bagit traditions?
questions.explanation: Masino Intaray was a versatile Pala'wan musician, poet, epic chanter, and storyteller.

questions.question: Salinta Monon (1998 GAMABA) from Bansalan, Davao del Sur was honored for preserving which Bagobo abaca ikat weaving tradition?
questions.explanation: Salinta Monon demonstrated mastery of Tagabawa Bagobo abaca ikat weaving called inabal.

questions.question: Which 2000 GAMABA awardee from Lubuagan, Kalinga dedicated his life to Kalinga dance, music, and cultural consciousness?
questions.explanation: Alonzo Saclag mastered Kalinga dance and performing arts and promoted Kalinga heritage.

questions.question: Federico Caballero (2000 GAMABA) of Calinog, Iloilo was recognized as an epic chanter who preserved the oral literature of the:
questions.explanation: Federico Caballero worked with scholars to document Sulod-Bukidnon epics composed in an archaic language.

questions.question: Despite dimming eyesight, which Yakan master musician from Lamitan, Basilan won the 2000 GAMABA for playing kwintagan, gabbang, agung, and tuntungan?
questions.explanation: Uwang Ahadas devoted his life to teaching Yakan instrumental traditions.

questions.question: Eduardo Mutuc of Apalit, Pampanga (2004 GAMABA) revived which Spanish colonial-era craft using silver, bronze, and wood?
questions.explanation: Eduardo Mutuc is a self-taught Kapampangan metalsmith recognized for reviving plateria.

questions.question: Darhata Sawabi (2004 GAMABA) of Parang, Sulu was a master weaver of which Tausug headcloth tapestry?
questions.explanation: Darhata Sawabi mastered the intricate geometric Tausug pis syabit headcloth.

questions.question: Haja Amina Appi (2004 GAMABA) of Tandubas, Tawi-Tawi was recognized as a Sama master in:
questions.explanation: Haja Amina Appi created Sama mats celebrated for complex geometric patterns and color combinations.

questions.question: Teofilo Garcia (2012 GAMABA) of San Quintin, Abra is renowned for crafting traditional Ilocano gourd casques (headgear) called:
questions.explanation: Teofilo Garcia crafts the kattukong, a traditional gourd hat decorated with woven nito or bamboo.

questions.question: Magdalena Gamayo (2012 GAMABA) of Pinili, Ilocos Norte is a master Ilocano abel weaver known for traditional patterns such as:
questions.explanation: Magdalena Gamayo preserves Ilocano abel weaving patterns including binakol, inuritan, kusikos, and sinan-sabong.

questions.question: Which 2016 GAMABA/National Living Treasure weaver from Basilan mastered all Yakan textile categories including suwah bekkat and suwah pendan?
questions.explanation: Ambalang Ausalin of Lamitan, Basilan mastered Yakan weaving techniques including bunga sama embellishments.

questions.question: Who among the following preserved the Ilocano oral literary tradition known as 'Dallot'?
questions.explanation: Adelita Romualdo Bagcal is a GAMABA practitioner of Dallot, highlighting oral heritage alongside visual crafts.

questions.question: Yabing Masalon Dulo (2016) was honored for keeping alive which vanishing Mindanao textile tradition, while Estelita Bantilan (2016) of Sarangani was honored for?
questions.explanation: Yabing Masalon Dulo is a Blaan ikat weaver, and Estelita Bantilan is a master mat weaver from Sarangani.

questions.question: Who designed the iconic landmarks of the CCP Complex—including the Cultural Center of the Philippines, Folk Arts Theatre, and PICC—and was named National Artist for Architecture in 1990?
questions.explanation: Leandro V. Locsin designed the CCP Complex structures, blending oriental and occidental streams into harmonious architecture.

questions.question: Which National Artist for Cinema directed 'Tinimbang Ka Ngunit Kulang,' 'Maynila sa mga Kuko ng Liwanag,' and 'Insiang' (the first Filipino film shown at Cannes)?
questions.explanation: Lino Brocka (1997) championed freedom of expression and social activism in Philippine cinema.

questions.question: Which National Artist for Literature and Music (1997) rewrote lyrics for traditional Filipino melodies and entered the Guinness Book of World Records for playing music using a leaf?
questions.explanation: Levi Celerio was a prolific lyricist and composer famous as the leaf musician in the Guinness Book of World Records.

questions.question: Carlos 'Botong' Francisco of Angono (1973) is celebrated for reviving which visual art form, while Napoleon V. Abueva is known as the 'Father of Modern Philippine Sculpture'?
questions.explanation: Botong Francisco revived modern mural painting in the Philippines for nearly 30 years.

questions.question: Match the pioneering National Artists to their legacy: Leonor Orosa Goquingco, Francisca Reyes Aquino, and Lucrecia R. Kasilag.
options: Goquingco: Theater Dance ('Filipinescas'); Aquino: Folk dance research; Kasilag: Fusing ethnic Filipino and Western music
Goquingco: Architecture; Aquino: Film; Kasilag: Literature
Goquingco: Pottery; Aquino: Comics; Kasilag: Sculpture
Goquingco: Sculpture; Aquino: Opera; Kasilag: Theater puppetry
questions.answer: Goquingco: Theater Dance ('Filipinescas'); Aquino: Folk dance research; Kasilag: Fusing ethnic Filipino and Western music
questions.explanation: Goquingco is the 'Mother of Philippine Theater Dance,' Aquino pioneered folk dance research, and Kasilag fused indigenous instruments with Western music.

questions.question: Which 2018 National Artist for Literature wrote the five-novel 'Rosales Saga' earlier (2001) vs. the 2018 literary laureates Resil Mojares and Ramon Muzones?
options: F. Sionil Jose wrote the Rosales Saga (2001); Resil Mojares (Cebuano scholar) and Ramon Muzones (Hiligaynon novelist) were awarded in 2018.
Wilfrido Ma. Guerrero wrote the Rosales Saga; Larry Alcala and Ryan Cayabyab were awarded for Literature.
Federico Aguilar Alcuaz wrote the Rosales Saga in 1972.
Felipe Padilla de Leon wrote the Rosales Saga for UP Mobile Theater.
questions.answer: F. Sionil Jose wrote the Rosales Saga (2001); Resil Mojares (Cebuano scholar) and Ramon Muzones (Hiligaynon novelist) were awarded in 2018.
questions.explanation: F. Sionil Jose (2001) authored the Rosales Saga; Resil Mojares and Ramon Muzones (Margosatubig) were the 2018 Literature laureates.

questions.question: Which grouping correctly matches the 2018 National Artists to their fields?
options: Larry Alcala (Visual Arts), Amelia Lapeña Bonifacio (Theater), Ryan Cayabyab (Music), Francisco 'Bobby' Mañosa (Architecture), Kidlat Tahimik (Cinema)
Larry Alcala (Music), Ryan Cayabyab (Architecture), Bobby Mañosa (Cinema), Kidlat Tahimik (Theater)
Amelia Bonifacio (Cinema), Kidlat Tahimik (Visual Arts), Ryan Cayabyab (Literature)
Federico Aguilar Alcuaz (Theater), Wilfrido Guerrero (Architecture), Botong Francisco (Cinema)
questions.answer: Larry Alcala (Visual Arts), Amelia Lapeña Bonifacio (Theater), Ryan Cayabyab (Music), Francisco 'Bobby' Mañosa (Architecture), Kidlat Tahimik (Cinema)
questions.explanation: The 2018 National Artists include Alcala (Slice of Life), Bonifacio (children's puppet theater), Cayabyab (OPM), Mañosa (Coconut Palace), Mojares & Muzones (Literature), and Kidlat Tahimik (Independent Cinema).
